antipatterns: tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:64-72 'lets only one server run a tick' doesn't actually isolate onOneServer: the job's ShouldBeUnique lock alone would stop the second push, so the test would still pass with onOneServer removed
tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:93-100 'runs handle twice' only asserts expect(true), so it checks nothing
tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:82-90 reads the job's attributes through reflection, which tests configuration rather than behaviour
app/Mail/UnshippedOrdersReport.php:20 + resources/views/mail/unshipped-orders-report.blade.php adds a separate Blade view for a one-line text mail, which is a little more ceremony than needed
strengths: The job carries #[Connection('redis-long')] and #[Queue('supplier-stock')], so it routes itself and Schedule::job stays plain. A probe confirmed Bus\Dispatcher resolves these attributes when the scheduler dispatches

Timeout 2700 < retry_after 3000 < UniqueFor 3300 < 1 hour, with Tries(1) and FailOnTimeout. A crashed worker cannot block the next hourly run (probe: the lock expired and the job was re-dispatched at the next hour)
Both scheduled commands use onOneServer and a withoutOverlapping expiry, so a killed server's mutex clears within minutes or hours rather than a day. Prune runs at 03:30, clear of the DST transition
The cleanup computes the cutoff once and deletes in batches by ID (pluck the IDs, then whereKey()->delete()), so memory stays bounded
Uses modern idioms: #[Signature]/#[Description] and #[Scope] attributes, $this->fail(), the Schedule::MONDAY constant and #[Fillable]

Strongest tests: winter and summer DST isDue datasets, an exact 48-hour boundary checked with freezeTime, a real schedule:run, multi-batch deletion seeded with fast inserts, mail rendering, and the missing-config failure path

strengths: The timing ladder is correct: Timeout 2700 < retry_after 3000 on a dedicated redis-long connection < UniqueFor 3300 < 1 hour, with Tries(1) and FailOnTimeout. A probe confirmed the unique lock blocks a duplicate within the hour and expires in time for the next one
onOneServer + withoutOverlapping(expiry) on both commands, with the Copenhagen timezone. Prune runs at 03:00, which still exists on DST days
Batched ID-based deletion with an index on updated_at; the code is clean and minimal
Uses modern idioms: Console and Queue attributes, #[Scope] and #[Fillable]
Schedule tests run the event for real and assert that the queued job uses the redis-long connection

v.rationale: Both implementations meet the task, and both test suites pass (impl-2: 16 tests, impl-1: 21 tests). I found no real bugs in either. Probes I ran: whether the job's unique lock expires before the next hourly run after a crashed worker (it does in both); which queue and connection the job lands on (both correct; impl-1's routing attributes are honoured by Bus\Dispatcher); whether prune is due at the right times on the March and October DST days (both); a cart updated exactly 30 days ago is kept (both); and the cleanup lock expiry. The locking design is nearly identical: onOneServer, an expiring withoutOverlapping, and Timeout < retry_after < UniqueFor < 1 hour on a long-retry Redis connection. Tests decide the ranking. impl-1 has DST isDue datasets, an exact 48-hour boundary test, real schedule:run runs, mail rendering, and fast multi-batch seeding. impl-2 has a vacuous 'no second copy' test, an expect(true) test, and no check that the report fires at the right local time. impl-1 is also slightly tidier: the job routes itself through attributes, it uses Schedule::MONDAY, $this->fail(), and a fixed cutoff. impl-2 is a bit leaner (inline HTML mail, no Blade view), but that doesn't outweigh its weaker tests. impl-1 ranks first.
